utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I understand the parties have some procedural matters. Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Briefly, Your Honour. With leave of the Court, I'd like to introduce Mr. Dragan Ivetic. He is sitting in for this week as my interpreter. There may be a possibility of him coming on the team, but Jelena is doing some investigative work right now in Sarajevo, and so we of course need a way to communicate with the client, and this is what we arranged. So with leave of the Court, he will be sitting, attending court this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I see nothing objectionable in that. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just with this application that has to do with the next witness, VG-35. I would normally make it the practice before the witness testifies to inquire what protections they believe are necessary. In my discussions with this witness, she had been granted on the 20th of June of this year a pseudonym and that all of her testimony be taken in closed session. And that was based on, I believe, the course of termination that her testimony regarding being raped was something that was more appropriately in closed session. When I spoke with her over the weekend, she advised me that she would have no objection to the rest of her testimony -- she testifies about certain background material, and she also testifies she was an eyewitness to one of the counts in the indictment, the killing of Hajra Koric. So with the -- the Prosecution is now requesting the Chamber to amend its order of the 20th of June and require or order that her testimony be given with facial distortion and pseudonym but that it be given in open session, except for the part that deals with the sexual assault on her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll grant that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And with that, Your Honour, the Prosecution would call VG-35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Before you do that, I have two matters in respect of which the Chamber needs some clarifications from you, Mr. Groome. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So I have to ask the Prosecution to clarify whether they still intend to call Witness VG-17 because that witness is not in the list of witnesses. If you can't answer it now, then you can take time to do your research.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If I could double check, but I believe it is our intention to still call that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. The second matter is the application by the Prosecution on the 11th of April requesting that the mode of testimony of Witness VG-002 be converted from viva voce to Rule 92 bis, and this was granted on the 22nd of April. With regard to VG-002 and VG-022, the Trial Chamber's decision was that, in its view, "The Prosecution may enter in its witness list the change of the manner in which it wishes these witnesses to testify," and I'm here quoting from the decision. "However, whether the witnesses will ultimately be heard in the manner proposed will depend on the determination of motions pursuant to Rules 92 bis and 92 ter in respect of these witnesses." But the Prosecution has not filed a motion pursuant to 92 bis with respect to VG-002. On the 12th of September, 2008, the Prosecution notified the Chamber that VG-002 will appear as a witness on the 22nd of September, although his mode of testimony is noted as 92 bis. So the Prosecution is asked to explain what is the status of this witness and what statements or transcripts of prior testimony it seeks to add pursuant to Rule 92 bis or 92 ter. That's a matter that you can take under consideration, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may call the witness now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The Prosecution calls VG-35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit, and you may begin, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-35, the Court has just ordered a change in the way in which you will testify pursuant to my conveying the information about your wishes about how this testimony might be presented. Your face will be distorted, and we will refer to you at all times by VG-35, and certain portions of your testimony will be referred to in closed session. Can I ask that we begin your testimony by having you take a look at a sheet of paper. I'd ask that you look at that and tell us, is that your name on that sheet of paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is that your correct date of birth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that you sign your name to the document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And after it has been shown to Defence counsel and the Chamber, I would tender it as an exhibit under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P100, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, with permission of the Court, I would like to use leading questions to explore some of the background matters of the witness's evidence and matters which are not in controversy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic is on his feet, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we do have a matter of principle to raise in relation to leading questions, generally speaking. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, on all questions? I mean, there are some questions that I can imagine in respect of which you would not be raising any issue, some background issues. But if it is your -- if you're really saying that you don't wish any leading questions at all, then that, of course, is something which we'd have to take account of.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [In English] Your Honour, with your leave, as far as I understood, this witness will testify viva voce, but this witness also has got two statements which she gave to the OTP in 1998 and 2001, so that confused me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, in the circumstances, proceed in the ordinary way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-35, I want to draw your attention to the spring of 1992. Do you recall when the Uzice Corps entered -- the Uzice Corps of the Yugoslav People's Army arrived in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes, but it was in May.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what did you and your family do upon their arrival?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: I fled from Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where did you flee to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: To Medjedja.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did there come a time when you returned to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Several days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Prior to returning to Visegrad, did you receive information about the situation in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes. They told us that the Uzice Corps had arrived and that we could all go back home.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were you told anything about the security situation at that point after the Uzice Corps arrived in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: They said that it was safe to return to our homes and to our work assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where were you working at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: In a company.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us the name of the company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: TMP, Elplin.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was the general nature of the business of this company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: We fixed gas tanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you tell the Chamber where in the town the main office of this company was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: It was past the bus stop, and there was Centrotrans there where they had all the buses, and then once past that point, that's where my company was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you returned to your company, did you -- was your manager or your superior the same person as it was before the time you left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was the name of your new superior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Furtula Strajin.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was Furtula Strajin's ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: He was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did Mr. Furtula ever issue you with a piece of paper or document after you returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you summarise what that document was? What was the purpose of that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: These were the certificates that were issued to the Muslims. It was a pass for me to get to work every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And would you have to present that pass on your way to work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where would you have to present that pass?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Just before I reached the tunnel. That was near the old railway bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In the period of time after you returned to work, did you become increasingly concerned with your security and your ability to travel back and forth to work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were there a number of events that caused you this increased concern for the security of you and your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I draw your attention to an event -- did there come a time when someone brought a weapon into the company and this caused you some concern?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please describe the type of weapon and the circumstances surrounding it being brought into your place of business.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: A Serb walked into my office carrying a weapon. It was a weapon with legs. I'm not sure what you call that, a machine-gun, a rifle, something like that. I'm not really well-versed when it comes to weapons, but it was some sort of a weapon. He brought coupons for food, lunch coupons, and put them on my table, and he wanted money in exchange for those, which was something that I couldn't accommodate. Then Furtula went out and walked back with him to the office, but the machine-gun remained on my small side table. The door shut, and I couldn't hear what they were saying. He stayed for some time and then left the office --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: -- but the weapon remained on my desk.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you, during this period, did you know a person by the name of Ekrem Dzafic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Dzafic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did he also work in this company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were there times that you travelled back and forth from your home to work in Ekrem Dzafic's car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there another occasion what you received a call from your home regarding people who had entered your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes. I got a call from my son.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how old was your son at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Not even 9. He was 8 and a half. He hadn't yet turned 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what did your son tell you was happening at your home while you were at work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: He said, "Mum, when will you come home? Our place is full of soldiers."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you have another child as well as this boy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Another son. I had two sons.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was he younger than this son that you've mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes. The other one had just turned 2 at Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were both children frightened by this -- the presence of soldiers in the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, VG-35, was there a particular final event that made you realise you no longer could go to work at your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes. It was a difficult moment. It was difficult for me to hear my son cry. It caused me a great deal of pain. I looked out the window and the mosque was on fire near the Rzavski bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what did you conclude after watching the mosque in the town burning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: I realised that the Muslims were not meant to stay around any longer, and neither was I.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And after that day, did you ever return to work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: For what period of time did you return to work after that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Several times Strajin Furtula would send a car for me, a company car, then driven by Piro Andric.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And then at some point did you cease going to work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, at some point in time, did your husband flee Bikavac because he was fearful that Muslim men were being taken away and killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could you repeat that for me?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when your husband left Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Around when -- around what period of time did your husband leave Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: He left in May.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And why did he leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: He left for work.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you remain in Visegrad with your two sons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did anyone else remain behind in your household?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: My father-in-law and mother-in-law remained.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there a time you attempted to leave on a convoy with your father-in-law, your mother-in-law, and your two children but were refused?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Why were you not allowed to leave Visegrad on that convoy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Because my father-in-law and mother-in-law were not yet 65.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to draw your attention to the 26th of June and ask you, did there come a time during that day when you saw a Serb soldier outside your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us what area in Visegrad you lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Ban Polje, also known as Bikavac.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how many people were in front of your house on the 26th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: There was I, my children, my father-in-law, my mother-in-law, my sister-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. With respect to this Serb soldier, how many Serb soldiers were in front of your house on the 26th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Milan Lukic was there with an --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand the expression.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask you to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please repeat what you have just said for the benefit of the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was Milan Lukic with a small boy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-35, I notice that you're trembling. Are you okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes, I'm okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Feel free to put on your jacket if you're cold in this courtroom, or if there's any other way we can make you comfortable, please let us know. How old was the boy that was in front of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Very young. 15, perhaps. I can't remember, but it was a young boy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, your evidence is that it was Milan Lukic. How did you know the name of the person who was in front of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: That person introduced himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you have a conversation with that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes, with Milan.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what he said to you and what, if anything, you said to him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Milan asked me about my husband. I said my husband had left for work and that was all I knew. That's what I said. He asked me where I got my house, where I was working, that sort of thing. I told him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there any conversation about your workplace and your superior at work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: I told him where I worked, and then he told me he knew all about me because Strajin Furtula had told him. I said, "I have no reason to tell you any lies. What I'm telling you is the truth."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you and him discussed both your age and his age?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes. Milan told me that he was born in 1967. I told him about my age. I'm older than him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how long did this conversation last?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Not long. I was scared when I heard his name. It was difficult for me to keep track of the time. Half an hour, perhaps, but I can't be specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Why were you scared when you heard his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: I'd heard about him before, saying that he was doing some bad things in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what time of the day did this conversation take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: It was in the afternoon, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how far away was he from you during the time that you were having this conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: He was outside my house. There was a table made of wood outside and a plum tree right next to it. He was seated at this table, and I was squatting nearby. I didn't sit down with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And approximately how far were you where you were squatting from where he was sitting at the table?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: 10 to 20 centimetres, no more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And during the half-hour period of time that you've testified you had this conversation, were you able to see his face clearly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How did he arrive at your house, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: On foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when he left your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how did he leave your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: He just left. He walked away, as far as the junction, and I don't know where he went from there, or how.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the boy he was speaking to, what was -- the 15-year-old boy, what was his ethnicity, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: He was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did that boy remain when Milan Lukic left, or did he leave with Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: He left with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, during the course of your conversation with him, did he ask you questions regarding the whereabouts of your husband?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: When I told him I knew nothing about that, he said, "I'll check and I'll be back to tell you. If you're lying to me, I'll kill you." And I said, "I'm never afraid of the truth."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did he say that he would be back that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: He said he'd be back that evening, but he didn't return that evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I think it may be helpful to the Chamber if you explain a little bit about the location of the different houses in the area in which you lived. And my first question to you in this regard is whether in 1992 your street continued in both directions, or did it end abruptly shortly after your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: The streets started from a place we called the ditch up to the town centre. From the ditch to my junction, where my house was, there was a path leading there. There was one house first, and then my house was next, and there was this path leading to another two homes, but that's where it ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask the court officer or the usher to please call up 65 ter 175.10, a blank copy of that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If someone were to stand in the front doorway of your house, would the end of the street, this abrupt end of the road, be to the left or to the right? So standing in the house doorway looking out towards the road, would it end towards the left or to the right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: The end of the road from where I'm standing right now was on the left, between the two houses you can see there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to make some marks on this diagram, I'd ask maybe with the assistance of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, the photograph is fine as it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to let me finish my question to you before you make any mark. The first mark I'd like you to make is, would you please put "VG-35" on the bottom of the photograph in front of you so that we know that the marks on this were made by you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Here, you mean? Give me a second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is it not working? Your Honour, I have a hard copy. Perhaps, again, we'll go -- try the tried and true methods.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can we place a hard copy of this same exhibit on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-35, we're going to ask you to -- we're going to put an actual photograph to the table to your right, and then we'll ask you to make the markings on this. While that's being done, may I proceed and ask you a few questions. Are you familiar with the house owned by Meho Aljic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where is it in relation to your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: First, I'll explain where my house is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to ask you to take a look at the photograph on the table to your right. Take your time to take a look at it and see if you can recognise -- recognise what we're looking at. Before you make any marks, I'd ask you just to answer a few questions. Please don't make any marks yet. Is this a depiction or photograph of the Bikavac area in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to write "VG-35" on the bottom of the photograph to indicate that it's you that's making the markings on the photograph? The usher will assist you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I now ask you to circle the house that you lived in at the time and place "VG-35" inside that circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If the usher might move the photograph over a little bit. We can't see where the witness has made a mark. I'm sorry, are we now going to try it in e-court? Perhaps we'll just proceed since we've already begun to mark this up. Perhaps the director could zoom out a little bit, and we can see the house that the witness circled.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I'd ask you to -- on this photograph, are you able to indicate where the Aljic family lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: It looks a bit different here, the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If you're not able to -- I mean, this photograph was taken recently. If you're not able to clearly identify where the house is, then I'd ask you not to mark the diagram. Please only do it if you are certain.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: It was round about here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to draw that circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And would you put an "MA" -- an "MA" in that circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the last house that I'll ask you to identify, if you know, do you know where the Turjacanin family lived? And if you do, circle that house, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: [Marks] This one, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to put a "T" to indicate that location.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you've given testimony about seeing Milan Lukic in front of your house on the 26th of June. Can I ask you to draw a circle and put "ML" inside that circle to indicate where it was that Milan Lukic was at the time you had the conversation you just testified to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Outside the house. He was standing outside the door. The door is on this side.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I see you've put an "ML" in front of that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, we don't seem to get these markings. I don't see them on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's very faint. Could I ask -- I'm finished the witness with those diagrams. Could I ask they be shown to the Judges and see whether they are legible or whether the ink is -- the ink pen has a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Those are all the markings, VG-35, I'd ask you to make. Could I ask that it be shown to the Chamber to see if the Chamber's able to decipher it. If not, then we could try again on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Will that be sufficient, Your Honour? Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-35, I want to now draw your attention to the 27th of June, 1992, to the early morning hours. Did something unusual happen in the morning of the 27th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where were you -- approximately what time did something occur at your house on the 27th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Right after 5.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where were you at 5.00, at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: We were all asleep in the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Somebody was banging on the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did someone from your household answer the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: My mother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what happened when she answered the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Milan Lukic barged in together with Sredoje, and there was someone else, but I can't tell you who.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what happened when Milan -- you mentioned Sredoje. Who are you referring to when you say "Sredoje"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you know him prior to this day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: I know he worked in the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were you aware that your -- whether or not your husband knew him prior to this day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did your husband know Sredoje Lukic prior to this day?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave, is the entire direct examination going to be through leading questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is leading about the question "Did your husband know Sredoje Lukic prior to this day?"

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it was not this last question that's in issue, but most of the questions so far have been leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would disagree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, why have you not objected? I did not grant Mr. Groome permission to ask leading questions. I told him to proceed in the ordinary way. If you find a question is leading, then you can object to it. Let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-35, how was it that your husband knew Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: My husband was a waiter. Sredoje patronised the hotel where my husband worked. My husband waited at his table, brought him coffee.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you know Sredoje Lukic by name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When the men came into the house, what room of the house were you in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: The bedroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what happened when they entered the bedroom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: They started saying provocative, nasty things. If you really want me to be specific, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would ask you to say, as best you can remember, what it was they said. And I'd ask you, can you identify the person who said a particular statement rather than using the phrase "they"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Milan.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what did Milan say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: "Look at them sleeping. Good pussy here. They need fucking." He was laughing, and I was speechless. I didn't utter a word.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How far away was he from you when he made this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: He was so close, as someone can be close to you when they pull the covers off you. We slept fully dressed in our street clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you said -- the record records you as saying, as someone who pulled the covers off you. Did someone pull the bed covers off of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm sorry. Can my learned friend Mr. Groome give us a reference for these allegations we've heard just now?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm not clear what ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yeah, what do you mean by a reference?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Page number when the witness said that Milan Lukic pulled covers off.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I believe it's 20 -- do you see it now?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where was Sredoje Lukic at the time Milan Lukic pulled the covers off of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: If I remember well, he was standing behind Milan.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How long did they remain in the bedroom of your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: When fear gets hold of your mind, you can't really tell the time. Maybe 15 minutes, maybe half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there anything obstructing your view of Milan Lukic's face during this time that he was in your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you recognise him as the same person you had a conversation with in front of your house the day before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there anything obstructing Sredoje Lukic's face at the time he was in your bedroom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe how it was they came to leave? Did anything occur prior to them leaving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Milan kept laughing and then they left. They walked out of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what did you do after they left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: We couldn't sleep any more. We were waiting to see what would happen next.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when anyone returned to the house that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately what time did someone return to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: I think around 7.30, 8.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise. I at this time formally tender that photograph that the witness that marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The marked photograph becomes Exhibit P101, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who was it that returned to the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Milan Lukic came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you please describe what happened when he returned to your house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: He banged on the door. My mother-in-law opened the door. Milan asked for me. My mother-in-law came to me, stood in the doorway, and said, VG-35, Milan is asking for you. I came out. I stood on the doorstep.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: He said to me, "You have five minutes to get ready to come with me."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what, if anything, did you say to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Right. I'm sorry. First of all, I was thinking. I was thinking of running away from the doorstep so that he would kill me. Then I thought of my children, what they would become.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you run away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At this point in time was he alone, or was he with other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: He was alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: I told him, "I'm ready. I don't need to get any more ready."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what did he do when you told him that you were ready?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: He said, "Come with me and get into the car."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there a car in front of your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you recognise this car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you know the owner of this car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who owned this car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Ekrem Dzafic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you get into the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where in the car did you sit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: In the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did Milan Lukic get into the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where did he sit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Driver's seat.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recall anything about the backseat of that car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Please tell us what you remember about the backseat of that car.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: In the backseat of the car was a bottle of liquor. I glanced at it, and in the rearview mirror, Milan caught me looking at it. He said, "You mean to kill me?" I said, "I've never killed anyone in my life." Then he grabbed the bottle and put it in the passenger seat next to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did the car leave from in front of your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did you do as the car pulled away from your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: I just kept thinking of my children.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where did he drive the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: He told me -- he told me he knew where my husband was. He told me he knew I was waiting to be exchanged to see my husband.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you remember where it was he drove the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: He kept driving somewhere, stopping by the Megdan.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Prior to arriving at Megdan, did he stop at any other place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: He drove somewhere. My mind was not working. All I could think of were my children. He drove somewhere towards the SUP, the Secretariat of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where is the area that you're referring to as Megdan? Where is that in respect to Bikavac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Just above the church.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you stopped at a house in Megdan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you know the person who owned that house?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat? We did not understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Would you please repeat that, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a house belonging to Forta. Forta was the family name of that family, a Muslim house. A friend of mine used to live there, and I had been to that house before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did Milan Lukic do when he arrived at the Forta house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: He told me to get out of the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where did you go when you got out of the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Into the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Prior to going into the house, did you see anyone in the vicinity of the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I saw Lakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is that the name of a person who you knew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe the inside condition of that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was the condition of the inside of that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Horrific. Everything was ransacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did Milan Lukic make any comment with respect to the condition of the inside of that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes. He told me, "It's true, it's not a hotel. My apologies."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I'd ask that we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-35, on the trip back from the Forta house to your own home, did Milan Lukic say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did he say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: He said that I would have to tell my husband what he had done to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what did you respond?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: I said, "You didn't do anything at all. Just take me back to my children."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he say anything to you with respect to leaving Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did he say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: That I'd never get out of Visegrad alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened when you returned home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: My mother-in-law saw me. Let me say this first. When Milan took me back, when we were at the junction near my house, he told me to get off. I got off, and I never turned back. I expected that he would perhaps kill me. As I was nearing the door, my mother-in-law fainted immediately. I walked into the house. My children, my eldest son put his arms around me and said, "Mum, you're back," and I said, yes. I held them as tightly as I could. I kissed them, and I cried because I knew what this meant to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I now draw your attention to that afternoon of the 27th. Did there come a time when Milan Lukic once again returned to your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes, he returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And this time that he returned, was he alone or was he with other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: With a group of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the people that were in the group with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: I recognised two of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you tell us who -- the names of the people who you recognised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, around what time of the day was this when they returned this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Between 4.00 and 5.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When they returned this time, did Milan Lukic say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did he say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: "What are you crying for?" He laughed in my face.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did these men do in your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: They took all of my money and jewelry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How long were they at your house at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Sredoje left, but Milan stayed, and there was this third person whom I didn't know. They got all my jewelry and took it away. I gave whatever jewelry I had, and I also had a ring that I gave to them. It was a large ring. A necklace, a long one, with two heart-shaped lockets that symbolised my two sons; one was smaller, and the other was bigger. The bigger symbolised my older son, and the smaller heart-shaped locket symbolised my youngest son, and they took that away from me as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was your physical condition during this period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: It was difficult. I was considering suicide that day, committing suicide, but my mother-in-law saved me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when Milan Lukic left the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how did he leave the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: They walked out. We thought they all had left. All of a sudden I started freezing, and I had a fever. It was the 27th of June. The weather was nice and warm, but I was freezing with cold, probably on account of my fear and everything I had gone through that day. I told my mother-in-law, "Mother, go shut the door for us, please. I'm freezing." My mother-in-law stood up, and there was a man sitting at the doorstep, the man who was with Milan, the one I didn't recognise, the one who was with Milan Lukic, the one I didn't know. He was sitting out on our doorstep and --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: He told my mother-in-law, "Don't worry. I'm watching over you, and I'll shut the door for you." And then my mother-in-law returned. Fortunately, we weren't saying anything right then. After all, we were too scared to talk. We were just worried whether we would survive. That was our only concern.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you see whether or not Milan Lukic and the other men had a car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you see that car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you recognise that car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Whose car did you recognise that to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Behija Zukic's car.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you notice anything unusual about the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: I'm not sure I know what you mean. I'm not sure I understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there any music coming from the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you characterise the volume at which the music was coming from the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: This was music, we used to refer it to as kalesija or burska music, at least as far as I could tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When the car left, were you able to tell the direction in which the car went?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: The car drove past my doorstep, and perhaps I should explain how I saw the car. I was in my sitting room, and I could see the car drive by the house from there. I could see where the car pulled over.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where the car pulled over, were you still able to hear the music coming from the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes, because the door was open.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm about to move into a new area of questioning in the evening. I'm not sure what time the Court intended to take a break but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll take a break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-35, we left -- we took the break at the point in time when you were describing the Passat and hearing music from it. I now want to draw your attention to, during this period of time, were you aware that there were some refugees, Muslim refugees, also living in close proximity to your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you come to learn where those refugees came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Those refugees came from Zupa.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And this area of Zupa, is this an area north of Visegrad encompassing several smaller villages?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask that Prosecution Exhibit 101 be called up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And VG-35, this is a digital photograph of the photograph that you marked with your own hand earlier today. Can you see this on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you see the house that the refugees were living in on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to circle that house and write "Zupa" to indicate the location of those refugees.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: It's just below my house. You can't see it. It's Hasan Vilic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. So your testimony is that it's not depicted on this photograph but it's just below the house that you've marked as your own?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've mentioned when Milan Lukic returned to your home that he was in a Passat. Can I ask you to draw a circle --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Yes, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I checked the transcript. This witness never said Passat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That is right. I can't remember the witness saying "Passat."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The car that you mentioned earlier in your testimony, what again was the name of the owner of that car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Hija Zukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask you to draw a circle and put a "BZ" to indicate -- I'm sorry, "BZ1" to indicate where that car was the first time you saw it on the afternoon of the 27th.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Just above my house here, in this area, on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And if you would put a "BZ1" to indicate that being the first -- the location of the car the first time you saw it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you said that the car drove some distance from the house. Were you able to see where the car stopped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: The car remained where I drew the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And while it remained there, were you able to hear the music from the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes. The entrance door was open.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. I'm finished with this photograph. I would tender it, Your Honour, as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P102, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-35, sometime after Milan Lukic and the others left your house, did you hear anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did you hear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Terribly loud shooting. I knew that there were a few of our men in hiding, and I thought they were caught. There was a lot of shrieking and screaming.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: May I now draw your attention to 9.00 that evening, or approximately 9.00. Did there come a time when your mother-in-law asked you to look at something?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection; leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll rephrase that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yeah. "Did there come a time when your mother-in-law asked you something," if you want to be very technical. Witness, did your mother-in-law ask you anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What did she ask you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "See through the bathroom window. There's a large fire."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you go and look through the bathroom window?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe your observations to the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: It was a huge flame. I'd never seen a flame so high. I thought a house must be burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to tell from where you were whose house it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Not at that time. It was dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you hear anything at the time you saw this house on fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: There were no more cars. There was no more music.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time after you saw the fire that someone came to your door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately what time was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: After midnight, around 1.00 maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So this would be 1.00 a.m. on the 28th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who came to your door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Zehra Turjacanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe what happened when she came to your door?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic is on his feet. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we have a redaction in the transcript because this name is the name of Protected Witness 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I've informed the Court earlier, this witness has now declined any protections from the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened when this person came to the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: She banged on the door. My mother-in-law got up. We all jumped to our feet. My mother-in-law opened the door. We didn't turn on the light because we didn't dare to. Zehra told us that Milan Lukic had set everything on fire, that she had tried to save her sister, but she did not succeed, and her sister burned to death. I did not dare to look at her.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Why did you not dare to turn the light on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Because if the Serbian troops saw the light, they would know I was there. I just didn't dare to turn the light on for my own safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How long did Zehra remain at your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: She just told us, "Run away. They'll set you on fire, too." That was all, and then she left our doorstep.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know where she went after she left your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: She just told me, "I'm going around to see if there's anyone else here, to tell them to run away to save their necks."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The refugees that you've identified just a few minutes ago, did you ever see them again after this night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is it your belief that they perished in the fire that you saw that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you did see the location where the fire occurred and were able to identify whose house it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: After Zehra told me that Milan had set the people in Meho Aljic's house on fire, my children and my sister-in-law set out just to run away somewhere. We passed by that house. It's difficult to describe the smell of burnt bodies and burnt hair. We tried to leave Bikavac, but we didn't manage. We went back home.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to now ask you -- or change my line of questioning and ask you: Did you know a woman by the name of Hajra Koric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you present when she was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: As best you can remember, what day was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: It was in the month of July. I cannot tell you the exact day, somewhere between the 1st and the 5th.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where did this event take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: It happened in a settlement called Potok.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Why were you in Potok?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: I was trying to leave Visegrad, and I went from one house to another, hiding. That house was the closest one to the bus station.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Without naming -- were there other people in that house, and if you could answer this question without naming any of the people that were in the house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How many people were in the house, without naming any of the individuals.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: We were all women and children. Let me just count them without saying the names. So I was among them. I think we were 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I ask that we briefly go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when soldiers entered the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how many soldiers entered the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: There were a few. I can't tell you exactly. They chased us out of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where was Hajra Koric at the time these men entered the house, these soldiers entered the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: She was under the table, under the kitchen table.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've testified that the soldiers chased you out of the house. Where did you go when you left the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: We set out to go back up to Bikavac. These people -- the original people had disappeared, and then Milan Lukic came instead with his group, and they said, "Stop. You are surrounded."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Prior to the arrival of Milan Lukic, did Hajra Koric tell you anything about the whereabouts of her husband and her son?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes. Hajra then told us that Milan Lukic was after her husband and her son. She told us that her husband and son had gone to Belgrade to hide with family, somebody who was employed with the army, and they were actually hiding under some sheet of tin at her house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened when Milan Lukic stopped the group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: He was going around with another man looking for Hajra. He was going from woman to woman. He came to my sister-in-law. Milan said, "It's not her." Hajra was the last one in the row, and when Milan recognised her he pulled her out of our group.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: He asked, "Where is your husband?" She said, "Milan, I told you the truth. I don't know. He left for Belgrade. That's all I know." And he just laughed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: She started to approach him. She said, "Milan, son, you know very well that my husband is gone. I'm telling you the truth." Milan took his weapon and shot her in the chest.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened to Hajra Koric after she was shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: She fell to the ground. Milan laughed and said, "What is she doing?"

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Then he turned her over with his foot, and he shot her once again in the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to tell whether she died after being shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes. She gave no sign of life.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: As you sit here today, do you have a clear memory of what Milan Lukic looks like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I would object -- I would simply object to the suggestive nature of the identification process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: "Do you have a clear memory of what Milan Lukic looks like?" What is there to object to in that? Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Why is it that you have a clear memory?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, did she answer the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did she answer the question affirmatively? Oh, yes, she did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, she did. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Why do you say you have a clear memory of what he looks like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: When somebody inflicts on you such grief and destroys all your pride and self-confidence, you can never forget the face. You can never forget the person who inflicted such evil on you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to look around the courtroom and tell us whether you recognise any people here in the courtroom today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the record, usual objection for identification in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We note the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask them to stand up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask, rather than have anyone stand up in the courtroom, could I ask you to stand up, perhaps if that gives you a better ability to see whatever it is you want to see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that's the better course. The accused who is standing, he's to sit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Blue tie. Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recognise anyone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: I recognise Sredoje as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you indicate who you're referring to when you say "Sredoje" by describing where that person is sitting and what that person is wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: He is wearing glasses.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is there anything else about his clothing that you're able to describe?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: His tie is red with some sort of design, stripes or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You may sit down now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the record reflect that the witness has identified Milan Lukic and also identified Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions of this witness. Thank you, VG-35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, this is a witness who has --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just bring this to your attention. The witness has just asked the usher that she needs to have a moment of a break. She seems to be in distress.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll break for 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: --- Break taken at 4.41 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honour, but before the witness comes in, could I ask my learned friend Mr. Groome for the reference related to his previous words related to VG-114, Zehra Turjacanin, and protective measures. I didn't find in the transcript from today that he raised that issue. So could we have the reference, just to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: At some other time. Let me give the decision now in relation to the motion filed by the Defence of Milan Lukic on the 9th of September requesting the Chamber to order that the trial be heard four days per week. On the 12th of September, the Prosecution responded stating that the sitting schedule is a matter for the Trial Chamber's discretion. The Chamber has considered the submissions of the Defence and decides that the Trial Chamber will be heard four days per week, and it amends the schedule to the end of October. In arriving at this decision, the Chamber has taken note of the arguments put forward by the Defence; firstly, that for reasons of which the Trial Chamber is fully aware and at no fault of the current counsel, the Milan Lukic Defence team is in the unusual situation of only having lead counsel during the trial with no co-counsel. Combined with that, the accused Milan Lukic is the sole accused on a majority of the counts in the indictment. The Chamber observes, moreover, that the Prosecution has made good use of the provisions of Rule 92 ter, thus accelerating the pace at which witnesses appear in court and at which the Defence must prepare. The trial will not sit Tuesday, 16th September. This is pursuant to a request by the Prosecution to assist them with the scheduling of their witnesses; also, Friday, the 26th of September; Monday, the 29th of September; Friday, the 10th of October; Thursday, the 23rd of October; and Friday, the 31st of October. The above-mentioned are the days that the trial will not sit. The Chamber also grants the oral request of the Defence for a recess during the Prosecution case and schedules a break in the case between Monday, the 13th, to Wednesday, the 22nd of October. The parties - in particular, the Defence teams - are expected to use this time to complete their investigations and prepare their witnesses. Consequently and subject to the rule 98 bis decision, there will be no further break between the close of the Prosecution case and the commencement of the Defence cases if they are called upon to present a defence. And I should stress that all of these arrangements are subject to review and revision as the case progresses. Let the witness be brought in. Mr. Groome, you wanted to respond to Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During the course of my opening, I indicated that the witness no longer was requesting such measures. I will wait until the witness arrives here in The Hague before formally asking for a change in that, but she's made every indication to me that she no longer wishes protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We requested from OTP some statements for the further witnesses, for the further coming witnesses, which are redacted. For example, the statement of this witness is redacted in a part where the mention -- where is the mention the name of Zehra Turjacanin. So that is the reason why I raise that issue, and up until now we did not receive any unredacted statement. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure when this -- this document was disclosed, but I'll see to it that Mr. Cepic has the unredacted -- the version that does not redact this name as shortly after court as I am able to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, before we took the break, I had started to say something which I didn't conclude, and it is simply this, that this witness has obviously been through a very traumatic experience and you, of course, have every right and indeed a duty to put your case, the case of your client, fully and fairly. But I expect you to do so taking into account the trauma that this witness has experienced.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Good afternoon, VG-35.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: My name is Jason Alarid, and I represent Milan Lukic. And I hope to get through this with no disrespect to you because I recognise while you were speaking to us you've been through terrible pain, and being here today has caused you to relive that pain, and I do not want to hurt you any more. Can we try and get through this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, to go to the beginning of your testimony, it's my understanding that the first time that you came to understand or know who you believe Milan Lukic to be was that day of the 26th when you saw him talking to a young Serbian boy. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And of course, when you were asked to identify who Milan Lukic was, the lawyers stood up and started objecting. But of course, we got through that, didn't we?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And before you came here to The Hague, of course, and when you gave your statements in 1998 and 2001, you knew who the defendants in Visegrad were, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you knew the first defendant that was arrested and tried before the Tribunal was Mitar Vasiljevic; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when you were asked to give a clarification of your statement in 2001, that was because you might have been a witness in the Vasiljevic trial, but you were never, in fact, testified; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, did you ever testify in a courtroom like this with Mitar Vasiljevic sitting at a table such as behind myself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: This is the first time for me in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so even though they had talked to you in 2001, you did not have to face Mitar Vasiljevic in a courtroom; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: It's true. Nobody called me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And at the time that you were asked to do that, you did know who Mitar Vasiljevic was, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: I did know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And may I ask you, we did not get too much into this, but how long did you -- were you raised in the Visegrad area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: I completed my secondary school there. I got married, and I lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Were you born in Visegrad, too, or did you come there as a child?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: I wasn't born there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what caused you to come to Visegrad to spend your secondary school time there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: We only had an elementary school in my village, and there was a secondary school over in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And may I ask you what village you were raised in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: Dobrun.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when you came to Visegrad for secondary school, did you know Mitar Vasiljevic back then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-35
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you know his name, just from talk in the community?
